paragraphs.text: DSH Web GUI top recent-session tab strip and favorites drawer plugin
# dsh-browser-tab
English | 中文

A recent-session tab strip for the DSH Web GUI, shaped like browser tabs: every
session you open add

s a tab, clicking a tab switches to that session, and a tab
disappears only when you close it. Favor

ites are a drawer dropping from the right
end of that strip, the way a browser keeps its bookmarks —

and like a browser,
open tabs and bookmarks are two separate lists: closing a tab never removes its

bookmark. The tabs you close by hand are remembered too: a short `Recently
closed` list sits next t

o the favorites button, so a tab closed by mistake is
one click away from being reopened.
## Behaviour

- **Hover to reveal.** The strip is parked off-screen at the top edge. Move the
pointer into the top

10px band and it slides down; move away and it retracts
after 260ms. It never covers the conversati

on while you are reading.
- **Wide and centred.** The strip spans 90% of the viewport width, centred

on
the top edge, so a wide screen shows more tabs instead of the same narrow
column; the tab row sc

rolls inside it when they still do not fit.
- **Wheel scrolls the tabs.** With the pointer over the

tab row, the wheel moves
the tabs sideways instead of the page — one notch of vertical wheel travels

a
stretch of horizontal row, with no Shift needed, like a browser's tab bar. The
movement is not an

imated, and it only applies over the row itself: over the
favorites button or outside the strip the

wheel is left alone.
- **Automatic collection.** Opening a session (from the sidebar, a link, or a
f

resh session) adds its tab, in first-seen order.
- **Click to switch.** The current session's tab ca

rries a green dot; clicking
any other tab selects that session.
- **Three status markers.** One lead

ing slot, one mark at a time. A tab whose
agent turn is still executing turns a small soft-blue ring

before its title.
A tab whose turn finished while you were looking elsewhere keeps a small
static b

lue check in that same slot instead: the "answer landed, not seen
yet" reminder, which is what tells

a tab that has answered apart from one that
never ran. A tab whose session is waiting on you — a qu

estion or a plan review
the agent asked for — shows a small static blue question mark there instead,

because that turn cannot move until you reply. The question mark outranks both
turn facts (it is th

e one thing you have to act on) and a running turn outranks
the check. None of the three animates, a

nd with none of the three facts the tab
is plain. All three live on the tab strip only, never in the

conversation.
- **Close by hand.** A tab is removed only through its close button, so the
strip is

exactly the set of sessions you have not dismissed. That button is
also the only thing that writes t

he recently-closed list: a session that ends
[该节后续省略]
## Placement
Three additive registrations, none of them replacing a shipped entry:
| Slot | Surface |
| `shell.overlay` | The tab strip, above every column and outside their scroll containers. It also r

enders the `Recently closed` and `Favorites` buttons at its own right end. |
| `shell.overlay` | The

favorites drawer, a sibling of the strip in the same list slot. |
| `shell.overlay` | The recently-
closed drawer, a third sibling in that slot. |

The buttons are part of the strip rather than registrations of their own: they
belong to that one ro

w, at its right end and outside the scrolling tab row, and
keeping them there means each drawer hang

s off the strip's corner. Nothing is
added to the session header, so no shipped header seat is shado

wed. Each
registration is wrapped in its own `try`/`catch` — a failed mount degrades one
surface, it
never takes the shell down.

Each drawer and its button are separate mounts, so the open flags live in
`fav-drawer-state.ts` and

`hist-drawer-state.ts`, module-level observables that
are never persisted. The strip subscribes to b

oth: an open drawer pins the strip
on screen, since a parked strip would put that drawer's anchor ab

er pins the strip
on screen, since a parked strip would put that drawer's anchor above the
viewport.
## Architecture
| Half | File | Role |

| Host | `src/index.ts` | No-op. The feature is entirely client-side. |
| Client | `src/client/index
.ts` | Registers the dictionaries and mounts the three surfaces (strip, favorites drawer, closed-his

tory drawer), each in its own `try`/`catch`. |
| Client | `src/client/RecentTabs.tsx` | The React st
rip: one row of tabs, the two tail triggers, hover and drag state, inline rename, and the per-tab co

ntext menu. It also holds the strip on screen while either drawer is open. |
| Client | `src/client/
FavoriteButton.tsx` | The favorites trigger at the strip's right end: star glyph plus label, `aria-h

aspopup="dialog"` and `aria-expanded` bound to the drawer. |
| Client | `src/client/ClosedHistoryBut
ton.tsx` | The recently-closed trigger, one step to its left: neutral arrow glyph plus label, same d

ialog attributes. |
| Client | `src/client/FavoritesPanel.tsx` | The favorites drawer: anchors itsel
f to the trigger rectangle, pins the current session, draws the bookmark tree, creates and renames f

olders, drags rows vertically and files them into folders. |
| Client | `src/client/ClosedHistoryPan
el.tsx` | The recently-closed drawer: same anchoring, lists the hand-closed tabs newest first, reope

ns one on click and leaves a dead row listed but disabled. |
| Client | `src/client/fav-drawer-state
.ts` | Module-level open/closed flag shared by the favorites trigger, the strip and that drawer; pur

e UI state, never persisted. |
| Client | `src/client/hist-drawer-state.ts` | The same flag for the

recently-closed drawer; opening it closes the favorites one. |
| Client | `src/client/fav-folder-sta

te.ts` | Module-level set of expanded folders; pure UI state, never persisted. |
| Client | `src/cli
ent/use-current-session.ts` | The session view (selection, live ids, titles, run facts) shared by th

e strip and both drawers. |
| Client | `src/client/drag-place.ts` | Drop-side geometry: left/right f

or the strip row, top/bottom for the drawer column. |
| Client | `src/client/controller.ts` | Snapsh

ot owner over all three stored collections; notifies only on real changes. |
[该节后续省略]
## Rapid switching

Recording a session is idempotent: `recordTab` and the controller both return
the same snapshot refe

rence when an observation changes nothing, and they notify
subscribers only for a real change. Click

ing back and forth between two tabs
therefore cannot re-enter the render loop, which is what produce

d the earlier
flicker when the strip was a dynamic plugin.
